# Notes: "A Dead Reckoning" by T. W. Speight (Chambers's Journal, 1889; Gutenberg #57737)

Single book, 19 chapters, no separate BOOK headings. Story in one volume.

## Characters
- **Clara Brooke** (née Danby; formerly engaged/courted by George Crofton). Brunette, 22, black eyes, olive complexion. Wife of Gerald. Impulsive, tender.
- **Gerald Brooke**: owner of Beechley Towers (~14 miles from London), 26, tall, fair, reddish-brown hair/beard, dark-blue laughing eyes. Raised in Poland and Russia from age 5 to ~20; grandmother Polish. Joined a secret Society (Supreme Tribunal, "the Cause") at 18 in an underground room in Warsaw, eight years before the story. Ancestors fought at Cressy. Motto "Death before Dishonour." Income ~£6,000/yr.
- **Miss Jane Primby**: Clara's aunt, fresh-coloured spinster, age a secret, weak head, good heart; embroiderer; nervous about pistol shots. Once engaged to Captain Singleton (mentioned by Clara's aunt in ch.1 "when I was engaged to Captain Singleton"). Mentions Dean of Rathdrum, Major Pondicherry, Count de Bonnechose, Mr. Tubbins (brewer).
- **Lady Fanny ("Lady Fan") Dwyer**: Clara's school friend, six months older, worldly, merry. Husband **Algy (Dwyer)**, yachtsman, currently in Mediterranean/Cairo. Their "modus vivendi": not always together. Friend Miss Peckover of New York.
- **George Crofton**: Gerald's cousin, tall, thin, olive, black eyes/hair, small silky moustache, gash in upper lip showing a sharp tooth. Furtive, cruel. Disinherited by uncle; uncle's will left Beechley Towers to Gerald; George got £5,000 legacy. Loved Clara; she rejected him. Later marries Stephanie.
- **Baron Otto von Rosenberg**: ~40–55, tall, thin, iron-grey close-cropped hair, heavy moustache, gold-rimmed glasses, ex-diplomat (German Embassy, Paris; St Petersburg, where he betrayed a secret printing press four years earlier). Rents Beaulieu. Murdered 28 June (a Thursday), shot through heart in the châlet in his grounds, about 7 p.m.
- **M. Paul Karovsky**: Russian, ~30s, black hair parted in middle, piercing black eyes, long thin face, ivory complexion, no beard/moustache. Society emissary. Brother killed/died in silver mines chain (brother died on road). Delivered death sentence against Von Rosenberg; drew Gerald by lot. Later offers to personate Gerald (ch.XI); arrested in his place. Reappears at end (ch.XIX) and says sentence carried out, Gerald absolved.
- **Jules Picot** (also "Monsieur Picot"): mountebank/street tumbler, ~40–45, sallow, thin aquiline nose, long tangled black hair, black fierce eyes. Drum and Pandean pipes. Wife Marie (English, died six years earlier). Son **Henri Picot** (8–9, golden curls, blue eyes, fillet with silvered beads; "p'tit"). Picot's daughter **Stephanie Lagrange** (later Crofton's wife) fled Von Rosenberg, who had promised marriage. Picot later confesses to killing Von Rosenberg; found dead in cell, poisoned (phial in hollow heel). Henri died in the first week of the new year after an accident, two weeks later. Picot calls Clara "la belle madame" and Margery "Margot."
- **Stephanie (Steph) Lagrange / Mrs. George Crofton**: prominent in Ventelli Circus "Queen of the Haute Ecole," grey eyes, light silky hair, massive chin, splendid horsewoman. Signor Ventelli is her former employer. Is Picot's daughter (revealed ch.XVIII). Gambler's wife; plans robbery of jewellery box (Mr. Sturgess, London jeweller, bound for Lord Leamington's seat, box worth £20,000).
- **Margery Shook**: orphan, ~16–17, nut-brown hair, hazel eyes, witch-like uncanny laugh; formerly on canal barge (Mariar on the boat); ague; Clara rescued her. Calls Gerald "Muster Geril," Crofton "Muster Crofton," Drumley "Muster Drummle." Laundry worker at Beaulieu, then Clara's maid.
- **Bunce**: pompous majordomo/butler at Beechley Towers.
- **Dixon**: groom; reported murder news.
- **Mr. Tom Starkie**: red-haired, good-natured, 23–24; son of **Sir John Starkie** (JP, Penrhyn Court). Hid Gerald in "The Priest's Hole."
- **Superintendent J. Drumley** (King's Harold police); sergeant Tomlinson; Simcox; Pringle (Von Rosenberg's man); Dr. King; Dr. Preston.
- **Pedley**: discharged groom, saw half-burnt letter, carried to police.
- **Roger Chamfrey**: London friend, rented Yorkshire moor; sent Gerald as second-keeper under name "Mr. Davis." Head keeper **Timley** and wife.
- **Mrs. Purvis**: landlady of the Beechley Arms.
- **Euphrosyne Smith**: circus acquaintance.
- **Lucas**: Gerald's "mate" signalman at Cinder Pit Junction.
- **James Maynard** ("Gentleman Jim"), signalman; wife (Clara's cover name was "Maynard"). Actually Gerald is the signalman at Cinder Pit Junction, Clara lives at a cottage down the lane.
- **Slinkey**: ex-railway man, nervous, in the gang.
- **"Lardy Bill"**: sham clergyman / "Colonel Crofton" in jail; rogue.
- **Sturgess**: London jeweller giving evidence.
- **Captain Singleton**: Miss Primby's past suitor.

## Places
- Beechley Towers (Gerald's house, park, terrace, morning-room, blue room, gallery with suits of armour, Priest's Hole at Penrhyn Court).
- Beaulieu (Von Rosenberg's house, châlet, lodge-gates, plantation).
- King's Harold (market town; Beaulieu lodge; Thompson the farrier).
- Woodberry Station; Beechley Arms; Penrhyn Court.
- Linden Villa (Crofton house, NW London suburb).
- Pymm's Buildings, No. 5, Soho (court off a main thoroughfare; Medwin Street grocer).
- Tottenham Court Road pastry-cook.
- Cummerhays (northern town, terminus of branch line from Greenholme/Greenholm Station; Cinder Pit Junction; Overbarrow village; Mellingfield station; Seaton Park, Sir William's horses; Wheatsheaf Inn; town-hall; jail).
- Varley's Cottage (ruined, haunted by Varley's murder, gang rendezvous in spinney).
- Bulloo (where Margery ran from).

## Chronology (key events)
1. **24 April**, six months after marriage: Clara, Miss Primby, Lady Fan talk. Picot and Henri appear, begging on terrace; Bunce insults them; Clara gives cakes and a coin. Picot starts at mention of Von Rosenberg.
2. Gerald and Von Rosenberg practise pistol shooting. Gerald lends Von Rosenberg a gold-and-silver inlaid Indian pistol (gift from a Nawab). Von Rosenberg leaves, walks through park. Crofton arrives, quarrels with Clara, breaks miniature of Gerald under heel. Karovsky arrives; tells Gerald of death sentence; Gerald refuses; Karovsky: "Remember!"
3. Crofton with Stephanie at Beechley Arms; Stephanie meets Henri, learns of Picot's child.
4. **Late June (ten weeks after April)**: Gerald writes warning letter to Von Rosenberg, interrupted by news of murder (28 June, shot ~7 p.m.). Margery reports police coming; Tom Starkie warns; Clara lies to Drumley ("husband left for Woodberry Station"); Clara hides Gerald in hall armour; police search fails.
5. Crofton breaks Gerald's pistol? No — pistol found by police near châlet. Pedley's half-burnt letter used as evidence.
6. Gerald flees to Penrhyn Court Priest's Hole; later to Yorkshire moor as "Mr. Davis"; in August a visitor recognises him; he flees to London, dyes hair and moustache black.
7. Clara and Miss Primby meet Picot and Henri in Tottenham Court Road; Picot finds Pymm's Buildings flat.
8. Settled as "Mr. and Mrs. Stewart" at No. 5 Pymm's Buildings (Soho). Karovsky visits, offers money and escape; Gerald refuses. Police arrive; Karovsky offers to personate Gerald and is arrested. Crofton arrives, reveals he informed police; Picot binds and gags Crofton; Crofton burns free.
9. Crofton and Stephanie at Linden Villa; Crofton plots jewellery robbery (14 April; Lord Leamington's jewels).
10. **April, Cinder Pit Junction**: Lady Fan visits Clara and Gerald (Gerald is signalman via Algy's influence). Clara overhears Crofton's gang plan at Varley's Cottage; Margery fixes "singles" (fog-signals) on the line. Clara arrives late, finds Slinkey in box. Gerald captured by "Lardy Bill" and bound to tree; Clara frees him. Fog-signals stop train. Gang flees or is captured. Crofton shoots Gerald, denounces him; Gerald wounded in arm.
11. **Next morning, Cummerhays justice-room**: Picot confesses to killing Von Rosenberg; long narrative. Clara faints. Remanded. Crofton jailed; at night escapes through cell window (uncle "Colonel Crofton" = Lardy Bill visit). Picot found dead of poison in cell.
12. Stephanie reads paper; learns Picot is father; letter she wrote him from London never reached him.
13. **Six weeks later (Ch XIX)**: Return to Beechley Towers. Miss Primby, Lady Fan, Tom Starkie, Margery (now maid; new French kid shoes). Crofton shoots at Gerald from terrace window; a dark-cloaked figure (Karovsky) knocks his pistol away; Crofton dies, saying "Gerald Brooke, you have won the game!" Karovsky states the sentence was carried out; Gerald absolved. Ends "THE END."

## Notable quotes
- Clara: "Such happiness as mine is too perfect to last."
- Margery: "O mum, the polis is coming!"
- Picot: "Ah, monsieur, you and la belle madame will be happy again."
- Karovsky: "English to the backbone."
- Gerald: "Death before Dishonour."
